## Design

### 2026-10-10 – **October 10: created basic Starbie PCB**

**3.2h**

**October 10: created basic Starbie PCB**

I simply followed the the week 1 guide because I've never designed a PCB before.

here's what I got done:

- setup Kicad
- made my schematic
- made a PCB design
-  encountered over 50 errors at one point
- redid the PCB design a few times
- figured out how to add pictures
- added cute BMO graphics

I am  making BMO from adventure time so I made a rectangle and tried to get it as dense as possible while keeping the button layout simillar to his character. This led to me placing the micro-controller on the backside and right under the screen which was causing it to short out and be intersected. So I then had to move it to right under the LCD which significantly increased the PCB's size.

### 2026-10-11 – **October 11: finished PCB & set up firmware**

**2.83h**

**October 11: finished PCB & set up firmware**

Today I:

-installed and set up Arduino IDE
-researched best way to give my Starbie sound
-settled on a passive buzzer
-found and installed buzzer library
-added buzzer to PCB design
-designed my sprite for BMO

designing a sprite for BMO took much longer than I was expecting because I had to keep tweaking it, I think it looks pretty cute though.

 I didn't really edit the code much because I can't test it yet so all I did was what is in the week one guide. once it comes to the second half of the program I will customize the code a bunch
